problem: Existing VLN speaker models generate short, action-focused instructions with few object/landmark references, and RL training on n-gram metrics lets them game the metrics without producing better sentences.
motivation: Machine-generated instructions are used to augment VLN training data, but their quality is well below human annotations. Good instructions need landmarks, directions, region descriptions and turn-by-turn actions, so the speaker should exploit the environment's spatial and semantic structure and be trained with a reward that is not a hand-picked metric.
key_idea: Augment a Speaker-Follower-style encoder-decoder with action, structural (object location/size/distance) and semantic (object-relation-room) encodings, and train it with adversarial (inverse-RL) reward learning plus unlikelihood and temporal-alignment losses.
insight: Ablations on R2R val-unseen show that Path Mixing data plus the temporal alignment loss improve CIDEr, ROUGE and METEOR (#5 vs #2). Adversarial reward learning with a recurrent (GRU) reward model gives the best SPICE and BLEU-4 (24.8 and 33.8), better than a CNN reward model (24.3 and 30.3), which suggests temporal information matters for judging instructions. Object and action phrase counts show SAS mentions more objects and directions than LANA, though it still mentions fewer objects than humans. CIDEr drops even as SPICE rises, which the authors attribute to CIDEr rewarding lexical rather than semantic similarity.
method: Path Mixing: builds 162k new instruction-trajectory pairs by recombining FGR2R micro-instruction edges within the same house. It filters edges without noun/verb, requires nodes at most 3 m apart, and avoids loops.
Action parsing and Temporal Alignment Loss (TAL): spaCy extracts action phrases, and a BCE loss supervises the decoder attention to align action phrases with viewpoints.

Action, Structural and Semantic Encoding: action is [cos/sin of elevation and heading]. Structural encoding is Faster R-CNN object features, box location, and size and distance from the point cloud. Semantic encoding is GloVe triples (obj, ConceptNet relation, obj) plus (obj, in, room).
Panoramic Room-Object Attention: concatenates candidate, semantic and structural features, then applies attention queried by the action hidden state and an LSTM to give a panoramic knowledge feature.
Trajectory encoder and instruction decoder: a BiLSTM over actions with scaled-dot attention over visual features, and an LSTM decoder with attention over the visual-action context.

Adversarial Reward Learning: a GAN-style IRL setup (Reward-Boltzmann, after Wang 2018) where a CNN or GRU reward model separates human from generated instructions and the speaker policy is optimised by policy gradient. Both are trained alternately on top of teacher forcing.
Losses: LM (MLE) + sequence-level unlikelihood + TAL, weighted 2:1:1.

setting.backbone: LSTM encoder-decoder speaker (SAS) with ResNet-152 panoramic features and Faster R-CNN (Visual Genome) object features; GRU/CNN reward model
setting.training_data: R2R (or R4R) train set augmented with 162k Path Mixing pairs built from FGR2R; ConceptNet relations and Visual Genome detector
setting.observation: panoramic RGB with depth/point cloud for object size and distance, detected objects, action angles
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoint transitions given as ground-truth trajectory (instruction generation, no navigation)
setting.privileged: ground-truth trajectories and actions given as input; point cloud for object size and distance

numbers.backbone: SAS LSTM speaker with GRU reward model
numbers.extra: instruction generation metrics (not navigation); trained with Path Mixing augmentation, TAL and ARL; single run

results: SAS_ARL+TF raises SPICE on R2R val-unseen to 24.8 (vs LANA 22.6) and on R4R val-unseen to 28.1 (vs LANA 26.2). It also improves METEOR, ROUGE and BLEU-4, but CIDEr is lower than CCC and LANA (43.5 vs 46.1 and 45.7 on R2R val-unseen). Generated instructions contain 18.11% more object/landmark entities and 12.03% more action/direction phrases than LANA.
limitations: Evaluated only with automatic n-gram/SPICE metrics; no human evaluation, and CIDEr is lower than baselines
Limited data diversity and vocabulary shift between R2R splits; single run, no downstream navigation-agent evaluation
Still mentions fewer objects than humans; fails to align objects, rooms and actions in order for some paths
builds_on: Wang et al. 2018 (No Metrics Are Perfect, adversarial reward learning)
